# Results — Study 375 (VXX-Roll-Decay)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The famous **short-vol
carry**: hold a constant-notional **short** in a VIX-futures ETP and harvest the contango
**roll decay**. True `VXX` only has a clean yfinance history from 2018 (the iPath ETN was
redeemed & re-issued), so we short **VIXY** — the same constant-maturity short-dated
VIX-futures object with a continuous split-adjusted tape from 2011, named a VXX-equivalent
throughout. We measure the carry, charge it borrow + rebalancing costs, and then put it
under the only test that matters for a short-vol book: the **crash tail**. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — **VIXY** (VXX-equivalent short-vol ETP) + VIX term structure (`^VIX`, `^VIX3M`) + SPY (public, no key) |
| Window | 2011-01-04 → 2026-06-22 (**3,888** trading days; **15.5** years) |
| Book | constant-notional **short** in the ETP, rebalanced daily; book return = −(ETP daily return) |
| Roll-yield gauge | `^VIX3M / ^VIX` > 1 ⇒ **contango** (roll tailwind for the short); **92.3%** of days |
| Entry / costs | passive daily short; **borrow 3%/yr** + **2 bps/day** rebalancing turnover (one-way) |

> **Why VIXY, not VXX (named on the Signal axis).** The iPath `VXX` ETN matured and was
> reissued in Jan-2018, so a continuous auto-adjusted yfinance `VXX` series only begins in
> 2018 and would *miss Volmageddon* (5-Feb-2018) — the single most important data point for
> this study. **VIXY** (ProShares VIX Short-Term Futures ETF) tracks the *same* S&P
> 500 VIX Short-Term Futures index, has an unbroken split-adjusted tape from 2011, and
> **contains** Volmageddon, COVID and the 2024 unwind. It is the honest tradable proxy for
> "shorting VXX." Its split-adjusted price fell from **633,840 → 21.86** (×3.4e-5) over the
> window — the roll decay made visible.

## The signal — is the roll-decay carry real?

The short-carry book earns a positive daily mean. Because vol regimes persist (carry
returns are autocorrelated), we test with a **Newey-West (HAC, 21-lag)** t — an i.i.d. t
would overstate it — plus a distribution-free **sign-shuffle placebo** null.

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| daily mean (short carry) | **+0.171%** |
| HAC(21) *t* (mean > 0) | **2.51** |
| placebo *p* (sign-shuffle) | **0.0076** |
| days in contango | 92.3% |

**The carry clears the bar.** HAC *t* = **2.51** (> 2) and the sign-shuffle placebo puts
the observed mean in the right tail (*p* = **0.008**). The roll-decay carry is **statistically
real** — contango is the usual state, and each daily roll of the ETP genuinely bleeds value
into the short's pocket. On the Signal axis this is **REAL**.

## Could you trade it? — costs barely dent it; the *tail* is the story

| book | ann ret | ann vol | Sharpe | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | **+43.0%** | 69.9% | **0.62** | **−91.8%** |
| net (3% borrow + 2 bps/day) | **+35.1%** | 69.9% | **0.50** | **−93.1%** |

A 3% borrow + 2 bps/day shaves the Sharpe from 0.62 to **0.50** — survivable. But look at
the **drawdown** and the **tail**:

| tail metric | value |
|---|--:|
| daily skew | **−1.65** |
| daily excess kurtosis | **9.4** |
| worst single day | **−43.1%** (2024-08-05) |
| 1% daily VaR | −14.6% |
| 1% daily CVaR | −20.7% |

| worst 5 short-carry days | |
|---|--:|
| 2024-08-05 (yen-carry unwind) | **−43.1%** |
| 2020-03-16 (COVID) | −39.1% |
| 2018-02-05 (**Volmageddon**) | −34.2% |
| 2020-06-11 | −33.6% |
| 2020-03-09 | −27.4% |

A **constant-notional** short loses **43% in one day** and draws down **92%** peak-to-trough.
The single worst day (−43%) is more than *three* months of carry, gone by lunch. This is the
"steamroller": the carry is real, steady, and small; the loss is rare, violent, and
career-ending. A book sized to a meaningful Sharpe is sized to be **wiped out** in the next
spike. On the Tradability axis this is **FRAGILE**, sliding to MIRAGE the moment you size it
up.

## Robustness — conditioning helps the Sharpe, not the tail

**Contango-only** (short ON only when `VIX3M > VIX` at the prior close, a 1-day-lagged filter):

| book | net ann | net Sharpe | max DD | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| contango-only (net) | +39.7% | **0.67** | **−66.7%** | −1.30 | 3.60 |

Filtering out backwardation lifts the Sharpe to 0.67 and *trims* the worst drawdown to −67%
— but a **−67% drawdown and skew −1.3 is still un-allocatable**. You sidestep some crashes
(you're flat when the curve has already inverted) but not the *gap* crashes that strike from
contango (Volmageddon went contango→backwardation in hours).

**Borrow sensitivity** — the carry is a *borrow*-sensitive trade:

| short borrow fee | net ann | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0%/yr | +38.0% | 0.54 |
| 3%/yr | +35.1% | 0.50 |
| 10%/yr | +28.1% | 0.40 |
| **30%/yr** (crisis hard-to-borrow) | **+8.3%** | **0.12** |

During the very stress windows when the carry would pay most, VIX ETPs become **hard to
borrow** and fees spike — at a 30% fee the Sharpe collapses to **0.12**. The market charges
you for the carry exactly when you'd want it.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and the tail is built-in

A deterministic short-vol ETP with a **planted daily carry knob** and **3 injected crashes**:

| planted carry/day | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | Sharpe | skew | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0000** (no carry) | **−1.99** | **0.987** | −0.58 | −0.40 | −100% |
| **+0.0030** (large carry) | **+3.42** | **0.0001** | +0.99 | −0.40 | −76% |

With **no** planted carry the engine does **not** find a significant *positive* carry
(placebo *p* ≈ 0.99 — it never invents one); only a genuine planted carry drives HAC *t*
to 3.4 and *p* to 0.0001. And the injected crash stamps a **negative skew** on the book
**whatever** the carry — proving the harness reproduces the steamroller by construction, not
by luck. The control confirms the engine is honest in both directions.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The contango roll-decay carry is statistically real on the live tape:
  HAC(21) *t* = **2.51** (> 2), placebo *p* = **0.008**, daily mean **+0.171%**, with the
  ETP bleeding ×3.4e-5 over 15 years. This is a genuine risk premium, not a fluke. (Vehicle
  is **VIXY**, the continuous-tape VXX-equivalent — named on the axis.)
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Net Sharpe **0.50** survives borrow + costs *on paper*, but a
  constant-notional short carries skew **−1.65**, excess kurtosis **9.4**, a **−43%** single
  day and a **−92%** drawdown. Conditioning on contango lifts the Sharpe but leaves a −67%
  drawdown; crisis borrow fees gut the net return. Survives on paper, **un-allocatable at
  NAV scale** — and one size-up from ruin.
- **Free carry? — BUSTED.** The carry is *real* but it is **not a free lunch**: it is the
  premium for selling crash insurance. You are paid a steady nickel for standing in front of
  a steamroller, and the steamroller has run three times in fifteen years (Volmageddon, COVID,
  the 2024 unwind), each time taking a third-to-half of your book in a single session. Real
  carry, real steamroller.
